# Panel View Triplet Time-Course Analysis

```{r}
#| label: fig-cgm-triplet-panel
#| fig-cap: "Glucose levels time course - Grand average and triplet patterns (P07 excluded)"
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 8

# Prepare data for all triplets
triplets_all_panel <- c("DDD", "BDD", "DBD", "BBD", "DDB", "BDB", "DBB", "BBB")

df_all_triplets_cgm_for_panel <- data.frame()

for(triplet_type in triplets_all_panel) {
  df_triplet_cgm <- data.frame()
  
  for(p in participants_noP07) {
    sessions_3 <- get_triplet_session3(p, triplet_type)
    
    if(length(sessions_3) > 0) {
      for(s in sessions_3) {
        p_data <- cgm %>%
          filter(participant == p, session_num == s) %>%
          filter(!is.na(timestamp), !is.na(glucose)) %>%
          mutate(timestamp = ymd_hms(timestamp)) %>%
          arrange(timestamp) %>%
          mutate(
            minutes_elapsed = as.numeric(difftime(timestamp, min(timestamp), units = "mins")),
            time_block = floor(minutes_elapsed / 30) + 1
          ) %>%
          filter(time_block >= 1, time_block <= 10) %>%
          group_by(time_block) %>%
          summarise(
            cgm_30min = mean(glucose, na.rm = TRUE),
            participant = first(p),
            session_num = first(s),
            .groups = "drop"
          ) %>%
          mutate(triplet = triplet_type)
        
        df_triplet_cgm <- rbind(df_triplet_cgm, p_data)
      }
    }
  }
  
  df_triplet_cgm <- df_triplet_cgm %>%
    rename(block_num = time_block)
  
  df_all_triplets_cgm_for_panel <- rbind(df_all_triplets_cgm_for_panel, df_triplet_cgm)
}

# Calculate summary per triplet
triplet_summary_cgm_for_panel <- df_all_triplets_cgm_for_panel %>%
  group_by(triplet, block_num) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_cgm = mean(cgm_30min, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_cgm = sd(cgm_30min, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    triplet = factor(triplet, levels = triplets_all_panel),
    triplet_type = ifelse(substr(triplet, 3, 3) == "D", "Dim", "Bright")
  )

# Unified Y-axis limits
y_min_cgm_unified <- floor(min(triplet_summary_cgm_for_panel$mean_cgm - triplet_summary_cgm_for_panel$sd_cgm, 
                               na.rm = TRUE) / 5) * 5 - 5
y_max_cgm_unified <- ceiling(max(triplet_summary_cgm_for_panel$mean_cgm + triplet_summary_cgm_for_panel$sd_cgm, 
                                 na.rm = TRUE) / 5) * 5 + 5

# Function to create triplet plot
create_triplet_plot_cgm <- function(triplet_name, show_x = FALSE, show_y = TRUE) {
  data_triplet <- triplet_summary_cgm_for_panel %>%
    filter(triplet == triplet_name)
  
  triplet_third <- substr(triplet_name, 3, 3)
  intervention_color <- ifelse(triplet_third == "D", "#F5F5F5", "#FFF9E6")
  intervention_alpha <- ifelse(triplet_third == "D", 0.4, 0.8)
  
  triplet_first_two <- substr(triplet_name, 1, 2)
  triplet_label <- paste0(triplet_first_two, "**", triplet_third, "**")
  
  x_labels_with_hbt <- c(
    "B1\n(5.25h)", "B2", "B3\n(4.25h)", "B4", "B5\n(3.25h)", 
    "B6", "B7\n(2.25h)", "B8", "B9\n(1.25h)", "B10"
  )
  
  ggplot(data_triplet, aes(x = block_num, y = mean_cgm)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = 6.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
             fill = "#F5F5F5", alpha = 0.4) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 6.5, xmax = 9.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
             fill = intervention_color, alpha = intervention_alpha) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 9.5, xmax = 10.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
             fill = "#F5F5F5", alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean_cgm - sd_cgm, 
                    ymax = mean_cgm + sd_cgm),
                alpha = 0.15, fill = "grey40") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = "black") +
    geom_point(size = 2.5, shape = 16, color = "black") +
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = 1:10,
      labels = if(show_x) x_labels_with_hbt else 1:10,
      limits = c(0.5, 10.5),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_min_cgm_unified, y_max_cgm_unified), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(
      title = triplet_label,
      x = NULL,
      y = if(show_y) "Mean glucose\n± SD (mg/dL)" else NULL
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_markdown(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 5)),
      axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 9),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = if(show_x) 7 else 8, margin = margin(t = 3)),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 5)),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, if(show_x) 8 else 5, 5)
    )
}

# Create D-ending triplet plots (no x-axis labels)
p_DDD_cgm <- create_triplet_plot_cgm("DDD", show_x = FALSE, show_y = TRUE)
p_BDD_cgm <- create_triplet_plot_cgm("BDD", show_x = FALSE, show_y = FALSE)
p_DBD_cgm <- create_triplet_plot_cgm("DBD", show_x = FALSE, show_y = FALSE)
p_BBD_cgm <- create_triplet_plot_cgm("BBD", show_x = FALSE, show_y = FALSE)

# Create B-ending triplet plots (with x-axis labels)
p_DDB_cgm <- create_triplet_plot_cgm("DDB", show_x = TRUE, show_y = TRUE)
p_BDB_cgm <- create_triplet_plot_cgm("BDB", show_x = TRUE, show_y = FALSE)
p_DBB_cgm <- create_triplet_plot_cgm("DBB", show_x = TRUE, show_y = FALSE)

# Grand Average plot

  annotate("rect", xmin = 9.5, xmax = 10.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#F5F5F5", alpha = 0.4) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 6.5, xmax = 9.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#FFF9E6", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean_cgm - se_cgm,
                  ymax = mean_cgm + se_cgm),
              alpha = 0.1, color = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, shape = 16) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Bright" = "#F5A623", "Dim" = "#4A90E2"),
    labels = c("Bright" = "Bright (1000lx)", "Dim" = "Dim (10lx)")
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Bright" = "#F5A623", "Dim" = "#4A90E2"),
    labels = c("Bright" = "Bright (1000lx)", "Dim" = "Dim (10lx)")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:10,
    labels = 1:10,
    limits = c(0.5, 10.5),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_min_cgm_unified, y_max_cgm_unified), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title = "Grand Average",

  guides(

    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),

# Empty spacer
p_spacer <- ggplot() + theme_void()

# Combine in layout
(p_DDD_cgm | p_BDD_cgm | p_DBD_cgm | p_BBD_cgm | p_grand_cgm) /
```

# Statistical Analysis

## Prepare the dataset for statistical analysis

```{r}
# Define Study Parameters for CGM

# Define participant list and light patterns
participant_list <- c("P01", "P02", "P03", "P04", "P05", "P06", "P07", "P09", "P10")

# Combine CGM data with light information
cgm_lmm <- map_dfr(participant_list, ~{
  df <- cgm %>% 
    filter(participant == .x) %>%
    group_by(participant, session_num) %>%
    slice(1) %>%  
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.na(cgm_intervention_mean), !is.na(cgm_intervention_cv)) %>%
    select(participant, session_num, cgm_intervention_mean, cgm_intervention_cv) %>%
    rename(participant_id = participant, exp_session = session_num)
  
  # Special light pattern assignment for P10 (missing session 5)
  if(.x == "P10") {
    light_df <- tibble(
      exp_session = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13),
      Light_Lag0 = c("D", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "B", "D", "D")
    )
  } else {
    light_df <- tibble(
      exp_session = seq_along(light_patterns[[.x]]),
      Light_Lag0 = light_patterns[[.x]]
    )
  }
  
  df <- df %>% 
    left_join(light_df, by = "exp_session")
  
  return(df)
})

# Build lagged light variables and filter valid triplets
cgm_lmm <- cgm_lmm %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  arrange(exp_session) %>%
  mutate(
    Light_Lag1 = lag(Light_Lag0, 1),
    Light_Lag2 = lag(Light_Lag0, 2)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(Light_Lag0) & !is.na(Light_Lag1) & !is.na(Light_Lag2)) %>%
  filter(!(participant_id == "P10" & exp_session %in% c(6, 7))) %>%
  mutate(
    Light_Lag0_num = ifelse(Light_Lag0 == "D", 0, 1),
    Light_Lag1_num = ifelse(Light_Lag1 == "D", 0, 1),
    Light_Lag2_num = ifelse(Light_Lag2 == "D", 0, 1)
  )

# Add participant demographics
participant_demographics_cgm <- tibble(
  participant_id = c("P01", "P02", "P03", "P04", "P05", "P06", "P07", "P09", "P10"),
  sex = c("female", "male", "female", "female", "male", "female", "female", "female", "male"),
  age = c(24, 21, 24, 23, 31, 23, 24, 28, 32),
  bmi = c(25.82645, 18.83239, 28.01022, 24.67550, 20.28651, 22.23099, 23.23346, 24.50895, 27.14304)
)

cgm_lmm <- cgm_lmm %>%
  left_join(participant_demographics_cgm, by = "participant_id")

# Apply exclusion criteria
cgm_lmm <- cgm_lmm %>%
  filter(participant_id != "P07")  # Exclude P07

# Keep only necessary variables
cgm_lmm <- cgm_lmm %>%
  dplyr::select(
    participant_id, exp_session, cgm_intervention_mean, cgm_intervention_cv,
    Light_Lag0, Light_Lag1, Light_Lag2,
    Light_Lag0_num, Light_Lag1_num, Light_Lag2_num,
    sex, age, bmi
  )
```

# Descriptive statistics for cgm_lmm dataset (mean glucose; CV)

```{r}
summary(cgm_lmm$cgm_intervention_mean)
data.frame(
  N = nrow(cgm_lmm),
  N_participants = length(unique(cgm_lmm$participant_id)),
  Mean = round(mean(cgm_lmm$cgm_intervention_mean, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
  SD = round(sd(cgm_lmm$cgm_intervention_mean, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
  Min = round(min(cgm_lmm$cgm_intervention_mean, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
  Max = round(max(cgm_lmm$cgm_intervention_mean, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
)

summary(cgm_lmm$cgm_intervention_cv)
data.frame(
  N = nrow(cgm_lmm),
  N_participants = length(unique(cgm_lmm$participant_id)),
  Mean = round(mean(cgm_lmm$cgm_intervention_cv, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
  SD = round(sd(cgm_lmm$cgm_intervention_cv, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
  Min = round(min(cgm_lmm$cgm_intervention_cv, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
  Max = round(max(cgm_lmm$cgm_intervention_cv, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
)
```

# Statistical analysis for mean interstitial glucose values

## Model building strategy

### Model m0: baseline (random intercept only)

This baseline model quantifies between-participant variability without any predictors.

```{r}
m0_cgm <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ 1 + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m0_cgm)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m0 <- confint(m0_cgm, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m0)
```

### Model m1a: add Light Lag 0 (current day)

This model adds the current day light exposure variable as a fixed effect with Light_Lag0_num.

```{r}
m1a_cgm <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m1a_cgm)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1a <- confint(m1a_cgm, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1a)
```

### Model m1b: add Light Lag 1 additionally (one day before)

This model adds the day before light exposure variable as a fixed effect with Light_Lag1_num.

```{r}
m1b_cgm <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m1b_cgm)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1b <- confint(m1b_cgm, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1b)
```

### Model m1c: add Light Lag 2 additionally (two days before)

This model adds the day before light exposure variable as a fixed effect with Light_Lag2_num.

```{r}
m1c_cgm <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num + Light_Lag2_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m1c_cgm)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1c <- confint(m1c_cgm, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1c)
```

## Likelihood Ratio Tests: lag effects

```{r}
# LRT 1: Does adding Lag 0 improve fit over baseline?
lrt_m0_vs_m1a_cgm <- anova(m0_cgm, m1a_cgm)

# LRT 2: Does adding Lag 1 improve fit over Lag 0 only?
lrt_m1a_vs_m1b_cgm <- anova(m1a_cgm, m1b_cgm)

# LRT 3: Does adding Lag 2 improve fit over Lag 0 + Lag 1?
lrt_m1b_vs_m1c_cgm <- anova(m1b_cgm, m1c_cgm)

# Display results
lrt_m0_vs_m1a_cgm
lrt_m1a_vs_m1b_cgm
lrt_m1b_vs_m1c_cgm
```

Interpretation Likelihood Ratio Tests lag effects:

-   LRT 1: Adding Lag 0 did not improve fit over the baseline model only (m0 vs. m1a: χ²=0.03926913, p=0.8429164)

-   LRT 2: Adding Lag 1 did not significantly improve fit over model m1a_cgm (m1a vs. m1b: χ²=0.08543069, p=0.7700685)

-   LRT 3: Adding Lag 2 did not significantly improve fit over model m1b_cgm (m1b vs. m1c: χ²=1.425619, p=0.2324808)

## Model m2: add linear session effect

This model adds a linear session term to account for potential temporal trends across the study.

```{r}
m2_cgm <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ 
    exp_session +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m2_cgm)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m2 <- confint(m2_cgm, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m2)
```

## Model m3: add quadratic session effect

This model tests for non-linear temporal trends (e.g., u-shaped patterns) across sessions.

```{r}
m3_cgm <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ 
    exp_session + I(exp_session^2) +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m3_cgm)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m3 <- confint(m3_cgm, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m3)
```

## Likelihood Ratio Tests: Session Effects

```{r}
# LRT 1: Does adding exp_session (linear) improve fit over baseline?
lrt_m0_vs_m2_cgm <- anova(m0_cgm, m2_cgm)

# LRT 2: Does adding quadratic term improve fit over linear only?
lrt_m2_vs_m3_cgm <- anova(m2_cgm, m3_cgm)

lrt_m0_vs_m2_cgm
lrt_m2_vs_m3_cgm
```

Interpretation Likelihood Ratio Tests session effects:

-   Adding a linear session term did not improve model fit over the baseline only model (m0 vs. m2: χ²=0.005565508, p=0.9405311)

-   Adding a quadratic session term did not improve model fit over model m2 (m2 vs. m3: χ²=1.122632, p=0.2893524)

## Model Selection Summary

Based on LRT results, model m0_cgm with the random intercept only was chosen as the final model. All other models did not find a significant light or session effects for mean interstitial glucose values in this group.

-   Model m1a_cgm: Lag 0 (β=0.4976, SE=2.5088, p=0.843); AIC=520.5, BIC=529.4

-   Model m1b_cgm: Lag 0 (β=0.4685, SE=2.5083, p=0.852); Lag 1 (β=-0.7339, SE=2.5083, p=0.771); AIC=522.5, BIC=533.5

-   Model m1c_cgm: Lag 0 (β=0.5860, SE=2.4828, p=0.814); Lag 1 (β=-0.8514, SE=2.4828, p=0.733); Lag 2 (β=2.9804, SE=2.4828, p=0.235); AIC=523.0, BIC=536.3

-   Model m2_cgm: Linear Session Term (β=-0.03617, SE=0.48413, p=0.941); AIC=520.6, BIC=529.4

-   Model m3_cgm: Quadratic Session Term (β=-0.2031, SE=0.1909, p=0.291); AIC=521.5, BIC=532.5

# Diagnostics summary

## Check 1: normality assumption for residuals

```{r}
# Q-Q Plot Residuals
qqnorm(resid(m0_cgm), main = "Q-Q Plot: Residuals")
qqline(resid(m0_cgm), col = "red")

# Shapiro-Wilk Test 
shapiro.test(resid(m0_cgm))

```

Interpretation: Normality assumption for residuals seems to be adequately met in the central region of the distribution. However some deviations in the upper tail need to be acknowledged with higher values than expected under normality assumption. Therefore, a sensitivity analysis excluding influential observations will be performed. Also Shpairo-Wilk normality test shows no evidence against the normality assumption for residuals (W=0.98601, p=0.656).

## Check 2: distribution of residuals

```{r}
# Histogram with Density Curve - Glucose Mean
ggplot(data.frame(residuals = resid(m0_cgm)), aes(x = residuals)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 20, 
                 fill = "#4A90E2", alpha = 0.7, color = "black") +
  geom_density(color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Residuals (m0_cgm_mean)",
       x = "Residuals", y = "Density") +
  theme_classic()
```

Interpretation: Residuals seem to be approximately normally distributed, however some slight right-skewness is visible.

## Check 3: normality of random effects

```{r}
# Q-Q Plot of Random Effects (Intercepts)
qqnorm(ranef(m0_cgm)$participant_id[,1], 
       main = "Q-Q Plot: Random Intercepts")
qqline(ranef(m0_cgm)$participant_id[,1], col = "red")
```

Interpretation Check 3 normality assumption for random intercepts: Acknowledging the limited interpretability due to the small number of random intercepts (n = 8), the assumption of normally distributed random effects appears to be reasonably met.

## Check 4: Variance Components and ICC

```{r}
# Intraclass Correlation Coefficient
icc(m0_cgm)
# Model Performance
model_performance(m0_cgm)
```

Interpretation Check 4 ICC: Approximately 25% of the total variance in mean glucose values is attributable to between-participant differences, while the remaining 75% reflect the within-participant differences

## Check 5: heteroscedasticity

```{r}
# Check for heteroscedasticity across participants
df_resid <- data.frame(
  participant_id = cgm_lmm$participant_id,
  residuals = resid(m0_cgm)
)

ggplot(df_resid, aes(x = participant_id, y = residuals)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#4A90E2", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Residuals by Participant (m0_cgm)",
       x = "Participant", y = "Residuals") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Levene’s test
leveneTest(resid(m0_cgm) ~ cgm_lmm$participant_id)
```

Interpretation Check 5 heteroscedasticity: Both visual inspection and Levene’s test results indicate adequate homogeneity of variance across groups (F = 1.87, p = 0.091). While the p-value approaches conventional significance thresholds, the homoscedasticity assumption is reasonably met. Visual inspection reveals that P04 and P06 show somewhat higher variance compared to other participants.

## Check 6: temporal patterns

```{r}
# Check for temporal patterns
df_resid_time <- data.frame(
  exp_session = cgm_lmm$exp_session,
  residuals = resid(m0_cgm)
)

ggplot(df_resid_time, aes(x = exp_session, y = residuals)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Residuals across Sessions (m0_cgm)",
       x = "Experimental Session", y = "Residuals") +
  theme_classic()
```

Interpretation Check 6 temporal patterns: Residuals show no systematic temporal trend (LOESS line remains flat around zero), indicating no time-dependent bias in model fit. However, variance heterogeneity across sessions is evident, with Sessions 11-13 showing substantially increased residual spread compared to Sessions 3-10. This heteroscedasticity likely reflects reduced sample size in later sessions (primarily P10). Several outliers are observed (particularly in Sessions 3-4 and 6-7), which will be addressed through Cook's distance analysis.

# Sensitivity analyses

## Sensitivity analysis 1: removal of influential observations

```{r}
# Identify influential observations
m1_cgm_mean <- lmer(cgm_intervention_mean ~ Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num + Light_Lag2_num + (1 | participant_id), data = cgm_lmm, REML = FALSE)

infl_cgm_mean <- influence(m1_cgm_mean, obs = TRUE)
cooks_d_cgm_mean <- cooks.distance(infl_cgm_mean)
threshold_cgm_mean <- 4/nrow(cgm_lmm)
influential_idx_mean <- which(cooks_d_cgm_mean > threshold_cgm_mean)

cat("Threshold:", round(threshold_cgm_mean, 4), "\n")
cat("N influential:", length(influential_idx_mean), "\n")

# Show influential cases
cgm_lmm[influential_idx_mean, c("participant_id", "exp_session", "cgm_intervention_mean")]

# Create robust dataset
cgm_lmm_robust <- cgm_lmm[-influential_idx_mean, ]

cat("\nOriginal n:", nrow(cgm_lmm), "\n")
cat("Robust n:", nrow(cgm_lmm_robust), "\n")

# Refit hierarchical model building strategy based on robust dataset (- 5 influential observations)
# m0_cgm_robust
m0_cgm_robust <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ 1 + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm_robust,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m0_cgm_robust)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m0_robust <- confint(m0_cgm_robust, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m0_robust)

# m1a_cgm_robust
m1a_cgm_robust <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm_robust,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m1a_cgm_robust)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1a_robust <- confint(m1a_cgm_robust, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1a_robust)

# m1b_cgm_robust
m1b_cgm_robust <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm_robust,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m1b_cgm_robust)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1b_robust <- confint(m1b_cgm_robust, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1b_robust)

# m1c_cgm_robust
m1c_cgm_robust <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num + Light_Lag2_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm_robust,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m1c_cgm_robust)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1c_robust <- confint(m1c_cgm_robust, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1c_robust)

# m2_cgm_robust
m2_cgm_robust <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ 
    exp_session +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm_robust,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m2_cgm_robust)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m2_robust <- confint(m2_cgm_robust, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m2_robust)

# m3_cgm_robust
m3_cgm_robust <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ 
    exp_session + I(exp_session^2) +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm_robust,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m3_cgm_robust)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m3_robust <- confint(m3_cgm_robust, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m3_robust)
```

Interpretation Sensitivity 1 removal of influential observations: Conclusions drawn from the hierarchical model building strategy with the entire dataset were not changed after using the robust dataset, where 5 influential observations were excluded (influence.ME package, threshold 4/n). No significant effects of controlled evening light exposure or number of experimental session days was found on mean glucose values during the intervention window in this population.

# Exploratory analyses

# Exploratory analysis 1: random slopes for Light_Lag0 (mean glucose)

Rationale: The primary model (m1) assumed that light effects are identical across all participants (fixed slopes). This exploratory analysis tested whether participants vary in their glucose response to current-evening light exposure by fitting random slopes for Light_Lag0.

```{r}
# Fit model with random slopes for Light_Lag0 using bobyqa optimizer
m1_cgm_mean_rs_lag0 <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num + Light_Lag2_num +
    (1 + Light_Lag0_num | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm, 
  REML = FALSE,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

summary(m1_cgm_mean_rs_lag0)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1_cgm_mean_rs_lag0 <- confint(m1_cgm_mean_rs_lag0, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1_cgm_mean_rs_lag0)

# Check for singularity
isSingular(m1_cgm_mean_rs_lag0)
```

Interpretation exploratory analysis 1 random slopes for Lag 0: The model with random slopes failed to converge (singular fit: perfect correlation between random intercept and random slope, Corr = -1.00). This indicates insufficient between-participant variation in light response, likely due to the small sample size (n=8 participants) and limited observations per participant.

## Exploratory analysis 2: fit GLMM with gamma sistribution and log link with cgm_cv_intervention as dependent variable

```{r}
# GLMM with Gamma distribution and log link for CV%

# Baseline model (m0)
m0_cgm_cv_gamma <- glmer(
  cgm_intervention_cv ~ 1 + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm,
  family = Gamma(link = "log")
)

summary(m0_cgm_cv_gamma)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m0_cgm_cv_gamma <- confint(m0_cgm_cv_gamma, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m0_cgm_cv_gamma)

# Add current light exposure (m1a)
m1a_cgm_cv_gamma <- glmer(
  cgm_intervention_cv ~ Light_Lag0_num +
  (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm,
  family = Gamma(link = "log")
)

summary(m1a_cgm_cv_gamma)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1a_cgm_cv_gamma <- confint(m1a_cgm_cv_gamma, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1a_cgm_cv_gamma)

# Add light exposure one day before (m1b)
m1b_cgm_cv_gamma <- glmer(
  cgm_intervention_cv ~ Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num +
  (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm,
  family = Gamma(link = "log")
)

summary(m1b_cgm_cv_gamma)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1b_cgm_cv_gamma <- confint(m1b_cgm_cv_gamma, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1b_cgm_cv_gamma)

# Add light exposure two days before (m1c)
m1c_cgm_cv_gamma <- glmer(
  cgm_intervention_cv ~ Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num + Light_Lag2_num +
  (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm,
  family = Gamma(link = "log")
)

summary(m1c_cgm_cv_gamma)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1c_cgm_cv_gamma <- confint(m1c_cgm_cv_gamma, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1c_cgm_cv_gamma)

# LRT tests
# LRT 1: Does adding Lag 0 improve fit over baseline?
lrt_m0__vs_m1a_cgm_cv_gamma <- anova(m0_cgm_cv_gamma, m1a_cgm_cv_gamma)

# LRT 2: Does adding Lag 1 improve fit over Lag 0 only?
lrt_m1a_vs_m1b_cgm_cv_gamma <- anova(m1a_cgm_cv_gamma, m1b_cgm_cv_gamma)

# LRT 3: Does adding Lag 2 improve fit over Lag 0 + Lag 1?
lrt_m1b_vs_m1c_cgm_cv_gamma <- anova(m1b_cgm_cv_gamma, m1c_cgm_cv_gamma)

# Display results
lrt_m0__vs_m1a_cgm_cv_gamma
lrt_m1a_vs_m1b_cgm_cv_gamma
lrt_m1b_vs_m1c_cgm_cv_gamma

# Add a linear session term to model m1a_cgm_cv_gamma
m2_cgm_cv_gamma <- glmer(
  cgm_intervention_cv ~ Light_Lag0_num + exp_session +
  (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm,
  family = Gamma(link = "log")
)

summary(m2_cgm_cv_gamma)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m2_cgm_cv_gamma <- confint(m2_cgm_cv_gamma, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m2_cgm_cv_gamma)


# Add a quadratic session term to model m1a_cgm_cv_gamma
m3_cgm_cv_gamma <- glmer(
  cgm_intervention_cv ~ Light_Lag0_num + exp_session + I(exp_session^2) +
  (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm,
  family = Gamma(link = "log")
)

summary(m3_cgm_cv_gamma)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m3_cgm_cv_gamma <- confint(m3_cgm_cv_gamma, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m3_cgm_cv_gamma)

# LRT 1: Does adding exp_session (linear) improve fit over baseline?
lrt_m1a_vs_m2_cgm_cv_gamma <- anova(m1a_cgm_cv_gamma, m2_cgm_cv_gamma)

lrt_m1a_vs_m2_cgm_cv_gamma

# LRT 2: Does adding exp_session (quadratic) improve fit over the linear session term?
lrt_m2_vs_m3_cgm_cv_gamma <- anova(m2_cgm_cv_gamma, m3_cgm_cv_gamma)
lrt_m2_vs_m3_cgm_cv_gamma 

# LRT 3: Is model m3 superior to model m1a?
lrt_m1a_vs_m3_cgm_cv_gamma <- anova(m1a_cgm_cv_gamma, m3_cgm_cv_gamma)
lrt_m1a_vs_m3_cgm_cv_gamma 

# Overview model fit m1a_cgm_cv_gamma
performance(m1a_cgm_cv_gamma)
```

Interpretation exploratory analysis 1 GLMM (gamma distribution, log link function) with CV as dependent variable:

Current evening bright light was consistently associated with less glycemic variation compared to current evening dim light exposure. No significant effect of the light exposure one or two days before, nor a linear session effect were found.

-   Model m1a: Bright light compared to dim light on the current evening was associated with a lower glycemic variability of around 22% (β=-0.2449, SE=0.1222, p=0.0451), AIC=301.2, BIC=310.0.

-   Model m1b: Current evening bright light significantly reduced CV (β=-0.2452, SE=0.1200, p=0.041), however no effect of evening light exposure one day before was found (β=-0.1797, SE=0.1214, p=0.139), AIC=301.0, BIC=312.1.

-   Model m1c: Current evening bright light significantly reduced CV (β=-0.24343, SE=0.11983, p=0.0422), however no effect of evening light exposure one day (β=-0.18893, SE=0.12238, p=0.1226) or two days before was found (β=0.06444, SE=0.12302, p=0.6004), AIC=302.8, BIC=316.0.

-   Model m2: Current evening bright light significantly reduced CV (β=-0.2448530, SE=0.1223774, p=0.0454), however no linear impact of the absolute number of experimental session days was visible (β=0.0001341, SE=0.0248313, p=0.9957), AIC=303.2, BIC=314.2.

## Exploratory analysis 3: age and sex moderation

Rationale: To test whether the mean interstitial glucose values are influenced by age or biological sex.

```{r}
# Fit model with age and sex 
# Center age
cgm_lmm <- cgm_lmm %>%
  mutate(age_c = age - mean(age, na.rm = TRUE))

# Moderation model 
cgm_moderation <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ 
    sex + age_c +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(cgm_moderation)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_cgm_moderation <- confint(cgm_moderation, method = "Wald")
print(ci_cgm_moderation)
```

Interpretation exploratory analysis 3 age and sex moderation: No statistically main effect was found of biological sex (male with female as reference category: β=3.3330, SE=5.3041, p=0.548) or age (centered: β=0.2580, SE=0.6771, p=0.713). As no statistically significant effects of the different light exposure variables or the experimental session number were found, no interactions between demographic factors and such fixed effects could be investigated.

## Exploratory analysis 4: light lag interactions

Rationale: Despite finding no significant main effects of light exposure on the current day or one or two days prior, all two-way interactions between the different Light Lags will be tested.

```{r}
cgm_interactions <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num * Light_Lag1_num + 
    Light_Lag0_num * Light_Lag2_num +
    Light_Lag1_num * Light_Lag2_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(cgm_interactions)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_cgm_interactions <- confint(cgm_interactions, method = "Wald")
print(ci_cgm_interactions)
```

Interpretation exploratory 4 Light Lag interactions: When including the interaction terms between the different Light Lags, the following results emerged:

Light Lag 0 x Light Lag 1 interaction: A significant positive interaction term between Lag 0 and Lag 1 was found (β=9.677, SE=4.791, p=0.0479). This interaction indicates that the combined effect of bright light on consecutive evenings (current evening + previous evening both bright) differs from the sum of their independent effects. Specifically, when both Lag 0 and Lag 1 are bright (vs. both dim), mean glucose is approximately 9.7 mg/dL higher than would be predicted from their additive effects alone.

Despite a marginal non-significant trend for Light Lag 1 (β=-7.201, SE=4.197, p=0.0915), all other effects and interactions were not statistically significant (p\>0.45). The positive interaction suggests a potential synergistic effect when bright light exposure occurs on consecutive evenings, though this finding should be interpreted cautiously given the exploratory nature of this analysis and the relatively small sample size.

## Exploratory analysis 5: persistence analaysis

Rationale: The persistence analysis for mean glucose values addresses the question: Does the number of consecutive days of the same light condition (run length) modulate glucose dynamics? This tests whether:

-   Dim nights: Multiple consecutive dim evenings produce cumulative effects on mean glucose values

-   Bright nights: Multiple consecutive bright evenings produce cumulative effects on mean glucose values

Key distinction from lag analysis: - Lag analysis: Tests whether Day\[t-1\], Day\[t-2\] each add independent effects - Persistence analysis: Tests whether being on the 1st vs. 2nd vs. 3rd+ consecutive day of the same condition matters

### Dataset preparation

```{r}
participant_list <- c("P01", "P02", "P03", "P04", "P05", "P06", "P09", "P10")

cgm_persistence <- map_dfr(participant_list, ~{
  df <- cgm %>% 
    filter(participant == .x) %>% 
    filter(!is.na(cgm_intervention_mean)) %>%
    # Aggregate by session
    group_by(participant, session_num) %>%
    summarise(cgm_intervention_mean = mean(cgm_intervention_mean, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    rename(participant_id = participant, exp_session = session_num)
  
  # Get light pattern
  pattern_vec <- light_patterns[[.x]]
  
  if (.x == "P10") {
    valid_sessions <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13)
    light_df <- tibble(
      exp_session = valid_sessions, 
      Light_Lag0 = pattern_vec
    )
  } else {
    light_df <- tibble(
      exp_session = seq_along(pattern_vec), 
      Light_Lag0 = pattern_vec
    )
  }
  
  df %>% left_join(light_df, by = "exp_session")
})

# Add demographics 
cgm_persistence <- cgm_persistence %>%
  left_join(participant_demographics_cgm, by = "participant_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Light_Lag0)) %>%
  filter(!(participant_id == "P10" & exp_session == 5)) %>%
  filter(participant_id != "P07") %>%  # Exclude P07
  arrange(participant_id, exp_session) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(
    condition_change = Light_Lag0 != lag(Light_Lag0, default = "CHANGE"),
    run_id = cumsum(condition_change),
    run_length = ave(run_id, run_id, FUN = seq_along),
    run_length_dim = ifelse(Light_Lag0 == "D", run_length, NA),
    run_length_bright = ifelse(Light_Lag0 == "B", run_length, NA),
    Light_Lag0_num = ifelse(Light_Lag0 == "D", 0, 1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    run_category_dim = factor(case_when(
      run_length_dim == 1 ~ "First",
      run_length_dim == 2 ~ "Second",
      run_length_dim >= 3 ~ "Third"
    ), levels = c("First", "Second", "Third")),
    run_category_bright = factor(case_when(
      run_length_bright == 1 ~ "First",
      run_length_bright == 2 ~ "Second",
      run_length_bright >= 3 ~ "Third"
    ), levels = c("First", "Second", "Third"))
  ) %>%
  select(participant_id, exp_session, cgm_intervention_mean, Light_Lag0, Light_Lag0_num,
         run_length, run_length_dim, run_length_bright, 
         run_category_dim, run_category_bright, sex, age, bmi)

# Display dataset
DT::datatable(
  cgm_persistence,
  options = list(
    pageLength = 20, 
    scrollX = TRUE, 
    order = list(list(0, 'asc'), list(1, 'asc'))
  ),
  caption = "CGM Persistence dataset with run-length encoding (P07 excluded, all sessions)",
  rownames = FALSE
) %>%
  DT::formatRound(columns = 'cgm_intervention_mean', digits = 1) %>%
  DT::formatRound(columns = 'bmi', digits = 2) %>%
  DT::formatStyle(
    'Light_Lag0', 
    backgroundColor = DT::styleEqual(c('D', 'B'), c('#e3f2fd', '#fff3e0'))
  )
```

## Model 1: linear persistence models, dim evenings

```{r}
# Dim Evenings (all sessions), linear
cgm_persistence_dim <- cgm_persistence %>% filter(!is.na(run_length_dim))

model_persistence_dim_numeric <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ run_length_dim + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_persistence_dim,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(model_persistence_dim_numeric)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_model_persistence_dim_numeric <- confint(model_persistence_dim_numeric, method = "Wald")
print(ci_model_persistence_dim_numeric)

# Dim Evenings without Session 1, linear
cgm_persistence_dim_no_s1 <- cgm_persistence %>% filter(!is.na(run_length_dim), exp_session > 1)

model_persistence_dim_no_s1 <- lmer(
  cgm_intervention_mean ~ run_length_dim + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cgm_persistence_dim_no_s1,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(model_persistence_dim_no_s1)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_model_persistence_dim_no_s1 <- confint(model_persistence_dim_no_s1, method = "Wald")
print(ci_model_persistence_dim_no_s1)
```

Interpretation exploratory 4 persistence, linear, dim: To test whether consecutive dim light evenings produce cumulative effects on mean interstitial glucose values during the light intervention window, the linear relationship between run length (number of consecutive dim evenings) and mean glucose values was examined. Two models were fitted, whilst the first model includes all observations, the second model excludes Session 1, as there is no controlled light exposure on the previous day, which might influence results.

Including Session 1 for dim evening analysis did not find a linear effect of consecutive dim evenings for mean glucose levels (β=1.770, SE=2.111, p=0.407).

Excluding Session 1 for dim evening analysis did not find a linear effect of consecutive dim evenings for mean glucose levels (β=2.475, SE=2.428, p=0.316).

```{r}
# Helper functions to extract coefficients from LMM
get_coef_lmm <- function(model, coef_name) {
  coefs <- summary(model)$coefficients
  if (coef_name %in% rownames(coefs)) {
    return(coefs[coef_name, "Estimate"])
  } else {
    return(NA)
  }
}

get_p_lmm <- function(model, coef_name) {
  coefs <- summary(model)$coefficients
  if (coef_name %in% rownames(coefs)) {
    return(coefs[coef_name, "Pr(>|t|)"])
  } else {
    return(NA)
  }
}
```

# Final model summary: m0_cgm

```{r}
# Extract components from m0_cgm
m0_cgm_coef <- summary(m0_cgm)$coefficients

# Variance components
vc_final_cgm <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m0_cgm))

cat("**Final Model: m0_cgm (Baseline - Random Intercept Only)**\n\n")

cat("**Fixed Effects:**\n")
cat("Intercept:", round(m0_cgm_coef["(Intercept)", "Estimate"], 3), "mg/dL\n")
cat("  SE:", round(m0_cgm_coef["(Intercept)", "Std. Error"], 3), "\n")
cat("  p:", format.pval(m0_cgm_coef["(Intercept)", "Pr(>|t|)"], digits = 3, eps = 0.001), "\n\n")

cat("**Variance Components:**\n")
cat("Between-participant (Random Intercept):", round(vc_final_cgm$vcov[1], 3), "\n")
cat("Within-participant (Residual):", round(vc_final_cgm$vcov[2], 3), "\n\n")

# Calculate ICC
icc_final_cgm <- vc_final_cgm$vcov[1] / (vc_final_cgm$vcov[1] + vc_final_cgm$vcov[2])
cat("ICC (Intraclass Correlation):", round(icc_final_cgm, 3), 
    paste0("(", round(icc_final_cgm * 100, 1), "% of variance between participants)"), "\n\n")

cat("**Model Fit:**\n")
cat("AIC:", round(AIC(m0_cgm), 1), "| BIC:", round(BIC(m0_cgm), 1), "\n")
cat("N obs:", nrow(cgm_lmm), "| N participants:", 
    length(unique(cgm_lmm$participant_id)), "\n")
cat("Family: Gaussian (identity link)\n\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-combined-cgm-mean-boxplots

  "DB" = "#F5A623", "BB" = "#F5A623"
)

# Labels with bold third letter
triplet_labels <- c(
  "DDD" = expression("DD"*bold("D")),
  "BDD" = expression("BD"*bold("D")),

  "BDB" = expression("BD"*bold("B")),

  "BBB" = expression("BB"*bold("B"))
)

# Colors based on third letter
triplet_colors <- c(
  "DDD" = "#4A90E2", "BDD" = "#4A90E2", "DBD" = "#4A90E2", "BBD" = "#4A90E2",
  "DDB" = "#F5A623", "BDB" = "#F5A623", "DBB" = "#F5A623", "BBB" = "#F5A623"
)

# Compute shared y-axis range across all four datasets
all_values <- c(
  df_plot_cgm_mean_noP07$mean_cgm,
  df_plot_cgm_mean_int_noP07$mean_cgm,
  df_plot_cgm_triplet_mean_noP07$mean_cgm,
  df_plot_cgm_triplet_mean_int_noP07$mean_cgm
)
y_min <- floor(min(all_values, na.rm = TRUE))
y_max <- ceiling(max(all_values, na.rm = TRUE))
y_breaks <- pretty(c(y_min, y_max), n = 6)

# --- Plot 1: Doublet 5h ---
p1 <- ggplot(df_plot_cgm_mean_noP07, aes(x = doublet, y = mean_cgm)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = doublet), outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, seed = 42),
             size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7, shape = 16) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = doublet_colors) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = doublet_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_min, y_max), breaks = y_breaks) +
  labs(
    title = "Doublets \u2013 5-h exposure",
    x = "Doublet",
    y = "Mean Glucose (mg/dL)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    aspect.ratio = 1,
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

# --- Plot 2: Doublet 1.5h ---
```
